account:
Today has been mostly routine, with some unverified talk about bridge, port, or delivery changes. I have not seen evidence of an actual disruption. The secretary reported that the builder found no confirmed hazard, work, or costs, that the innkeeper had only an unspecified rumour, and that the baker denied announcing crossing or delivery changes and confirmed normal operations. I do not know where the rumour began or whether it had any purpose beyond passing along uncertain news.

At the mill inspection I counted 128 hay bales in the sale chest. No shortage or delivery order was confirmed. Freight said the warehouse had been empty when checked and offered storage and transport, intending to ask the baker about a definite need before moving grain. That appears to be an offer to help, not evidence that a delivery is required. I authorized no grain transport. The neighbour has been passing along my clarification that no bridge or port change is confirmed.

I kept my lunch and afternoon appointments, including tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage, then returned to the office. The expected council letters have not appeared: the secretary says all four hall table chests were empty and there is no new urgent correspondence. This is an absence of expected business, not evidence of interference. The secretary needs a writable book to make the permanent office record, including the instruction about grain transport. I have just agreed to buy one at the market and return with it. My next scheduled destination is home at nineteen o'clock.
